probes.question: what does the pinned toolchain really emit for the fixture, and does it agree with the independent hand manifest?
probes.result: AGREES with manifest totals (5/7). Reproduced byte-identically on a second independent run from the committed asset.

probes.question: is the position range half-open, and can an end column of 1 occur?
probes.result: half-open PROVEN by shared boundary positions (28.22,29.2 ends where 29.2,31.3 begins). No end column of 1 in any gofmt-clean shape, including an unformatted switch whose closing brace sits at column 1 -- a case-clause body ends at its last statement (21.8,22.13), not at the following token.

probes.question: can an end column of 1 be produced at all, and does it discriminate the two candidate rules?
probes.result: PRODUCIBLE (6.24,7.1) but only in source gofmt rewrites, and it DISCRIMINATES NOTHING: the token ending the block at column 1 begins the next block, so both rules attribute the same lines {6,7,8,9,10}. Both still attribute line 6 (a func signature) and line 9 (a closing brace), neither of which is a statement.

probes.question: on the real two-commit diff, do the candidate rules and the manifest agree?
probes.result: CONTRADICTION. All three rules report 66.7% over DIFFERENT line sets, so a percentage-only oracle cannot tell them apart -- A-208's vacuous-agreement failure mode, in the Go setting. CORRECTED 2026-08-11: the sets are NOT disjoint. The manifest's covered set {22,25} is a strict subset of the inclusive rule's {21,...,26}, and {30} of {29,30,31}; block extent is a strict over-approximation of the statement-line set. The superset relation holds for the executable and executed sets but NOT for the missing set -- see P27-PROBE-9.

probes.question: what does the real module query return, for the adapter's module-path derivation?
probes.result: Exactly one Main:true object with one nonempty Path. Offline, no dependency resolution. Confirms the packet's resolve_go_adapter contract is implementable as written; the returned object also carries Dir/GoMod keys, which the adapter must tolerate without treating them as module identity.

probes.question: is the impossibility unconditional, or only a property of our four fixtures?
probes.result: UNCONDITIONAL. Both files compile and execute under go1.25.12 and emit BYTE-IDENTICAL profiles. A rule is a function of the profile; identical input forces identical output; the two correct answers differ; therefore every profile-only rule is wrong on at least one. Independently reproduced by the carver after the review reported it. This supersedes the four-witness argument as the proof of record.

probes.question: do the original four witnesses discriminate a wrong rule from a right one?
probes.result: NO. R1 matches the manifest exactly on all four original witnesses, so the original claim that they 'do not support one lossless rule' was FALSE -- they were non-discriminating, this project's A-143/A-150 class one layer up. R1 dies on seg.go, whose third block (7.2,8.4) is a MULTI-LINE block starting AT a statement, so its statement sits on startLine -- the opposite offset from the multi-line blocks above it. Every statement-start block among the original four was single-line, which is why the gap went unseen.

probes.question: is block extent a superset of the statement-line set for the MISSING set too?
probes.result: NO. Line 4 is 'f := func() int { return 7 }'. The literal's body block 4.18,4.30 never ran, but the enclosing 3.14,4.18 did, and executed-wins-on-overlap promotes line 4 to executed -- an uncovered statement laundered by a covered neighbour on the same line. So the over-approximation relation holds for the executable and executed sets but NOT for the missing set. Noted honestly: this particular collapse is line granularity's own limit and coverage.py shares it, unlike the comment and closing-brace over-attribution, which is specific to block extent.
